parts.text: A car accelerates uniformly in a straight line from rest at time t = 0. At t = 3.2 s, the speed of the car is 13.0 m / s.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (a) (i) Calculate the acceleration of the car. acceleration = ......................................................... [2]

ms.label: 1(a)(ii)
ms.text: (acceleration is) change / increase in velocity per unit time OR rate of change of velocity

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) The car travels at 13.0 m / s from t = 3.2 s to t = 12.0 s.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Plot the speed–time graph for the car from t = 0 to t = 12.0 s. 0 0 16.0 14.0 12.0 10.0 8.0 6.0 4.0 2.0 t / s speed m / s 14.0 12.0 10.0 8.0 6.0 4.0 2.0 [2]

ms.label: 1(b)(i)
ms.text:
straight line joining (0,0) and (3.2,13.0)
horizontal line from 3.2 s to 12.0 s

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Determine the distance travelled by the car between t = 0 and t = 3.2 s. distance = ......................................................... [2]

ms.label: 1(b)(ii)
ms.text:
21 m
area under speed-time graph (between 0 s and 3.2 s)
OR average velocity × time

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) The car decelerates from 13.0 m / s to 0 m / s at a constant deceleration. The mass of the car is 1350 kg. The car travels 13 m in 2.0 s as it decelerates. Show that the work done by the car as it decelerates is approximately 1.1 × 10 5 J. [4]

ms.label: 1(d)
ms.text:
any sensible suggestion that increases the stopping distance
explanation (to match suggestion)
